title: Texts in Time · Islamic Intellectual Atlas
mobile_interface_note: The main UI has Hanafi-inspired tabs By century, By region and Source network, with one subject selector and search. A georeferenced coastal map shows separately documented author and work events, and unplaced source records remain counted. Source network and book timeline remain available across sciences.
whole_range_note: Use the shared year controls and zoomable era clusters; switch sciences without changing map interface.
date_marker_note: Marker is a dated event, bound, uncertainty window or distinct editing stage; label width is non-temporal.
visual_modes: documented work composition and recension pins

chronology_enrichment.event_type: author death, not book composition or manuscript copying
chronology_enrichment.unplaced_workflow: Immediate searchable source workbench in both chronology and geographic views

geography.unplaced_research_caveat: No automatic geolocation from an author nisba, text title or manuscript catalogue association.

bibliography_map.mode: single shared chronological renderer with source-date qualifications, undated source-record lanes, Hanafi-style bidirectional work-centred networks and optional principal-texts synopses
graph_interactions: one shared year axis for all sciences
zoom and pan to era clusters
visible undated workbench and Arabic title/author search

textual_family_note: The 404/377 audited dataset remains unchanged and the earlier UI is archived. The geographic map has a small cited event sample (author biography vs text composition); it is not a complete geocoding of Alreq or OpenITI. No invented influence or manuscript dates.
pdf_note: The live atlas now includes subject-specific interactive SVG graphs of cited books, jurists and classical legal schools, including 2025 OpenITI work candidates and Alreq source catalogue entries. The revision 8 offline ZIP and older PDFs predate these additions; they are historical snapshots. Catalogue references are not acquired manuscript scans, verified complete texts or legal-opinion graphs.
reader_return_links: Preserve safe debate views, passage context, filters and comparison selection.
